_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Eritrea covering Aksumite heritage, Italian Eritrea, British administration, Ethiopian federation and annexation, 30-year liberation war, independence 1993, Isaias Afwerki's isolation, and Tigray War involvement.

country_profile.government_type: Unitary one-party presidential republic (de facto single-party state)

ethnic_groups.name: Tigrinya
ethnic_groups.notes: Highland Eritrea; largest group; Tigrinya-speaking; majority Orthodox Christian; historically dominant

ethnic_groups.name: Tigre
ethnic_groups.notes: Western and northern lowlands; Tigre-speaking; predominantly Muslim; semi-nomadic pastoralists

ethnic_groups.name: Saho
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern highlands and coast; Cushitic-speaking; mixed Muslim/Christian; pastoralists and agriculturalists

ethnic_groups.name: Kunama
ethnic_groups.notes: Gash-Barka region; Nilo-Saharan; among oldest inhabitants; agricultural; distinct from highland cultures

ethnic_groups.name: Rashaida
ethnic_groups.notes: Red Sea coast; Arabic-speaking; arrived from Saudi Arabia in 19th century; nomadic; maintain Arab identity

ethnic_groups.name: Bilen
ethnic_groups.notes: Keren area; Cushitic-speaking; mixed Muslim/Catholic; historically associated with Bogos region

ethnic_groups.name: Afar
ethnic_groups.notes: Dankalia/southern Red Sea coast; Cushitic pastoralists; cross-border with Djibouti and Ethiopia

ethnic_groups.name: Nara
ethnic_groups.notes: Gash-Barka; Nilo-Saharan; also called Baria; agriculturalists

ethnic_groups.name: Hedareb (Beja/T'bdawe)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern border; Cushitic; related to Sudanese Beja; pastoralists

natural_resources.notes: Bisha gold mine (Nevsun Resources, controversy over forced labour); potash deposits at Colluli (among world's shallowest, near surface); salt (Danakil Depression); Red Sea fishing rights; Danakil Depression geothermal potential

military.notes: Indefinite national service (nominally 18 months but often extends 10-20 years; de facto forced labour; primary driver of mass emigration); one of world's most militarized societies; fought Ethiopia 1998-2000 (100k killed); rapprochement with Ethiopia 2018 (Abiy Nobel Prize) but border still disputed

infrastructure.notes: No 4G; only 2G mobile; EriTel state monopoly; one of world's least connected countries.

press_freedom_index.note: Dead last globally, worst press freedom in world

natural_hazards: volcanic/geothermal (Danakil, one of most volcanically active regions globally)

debt_aid.notes: One of highest debt-to-GDP ratios globally; limited engagement with international financial institutions; sanctions era (2009-2018, UN arms embargo); self-reliance ideology limits aid acceptance; 2% diaspora tax controversial

top_universities: Eritrea Institute of Technology (replaced University of Asmara, closed 2006)
education.notes: University of Asmara (1958, one of Africa's oldest) closed and replaced by scattered colleges; militarization of education (final year at Sawa military camp); nine ethnic languages taught in primary; brain drain catastrophic (~5,000 flee monthly)

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 1.0 million (Sudan, Ethiopia, Israel, Germany, Sweden, UK, USA)
diaspora_migration.notes: One of world's top refugee-producing countries per capita; indefinite conscription primary driver; ~5,000 flee monthly via Sudan/Ethiopia routes; Mediterranean crossing deaths; 2% 'recovery and rehabilitation tax' on diaspora (controversially enforced); diaspora politically split pro/anti-Isaias

digital_economy.notes: One of least connected countries globally; EriTel government monopoly; internet penetration ~7% (among world's lowest); no private media; no mobile money; no tech ecosystem; isolation policies prevent digital development

country_profile.notes_unique: Won independence from Ethiopia in 1993 after a 30-year guerrilla war; the capital Asmara's Modernist architecture is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

geography.terrain: Central highlands; western lowlands; eastern coastal desert strip; Danakil Depression in southeast
geography.notes: Part of Horn of Africa; Dahlak Archipelago in Red Sea; Danakil Depression has hottest average temperatures on Earth; 1200km Red Sea coastline.

economy_extended.notes: Heavily militarized economy; diaspora tax (2%); Bisha gold/copper mine (Nevsun/Zijin Mining); port access leverage over Ethiopia lost in 1998 war.

health.notes: Community-based health system; good vaccination coverage despite poverty; severe doctor shortage; national service doctors.

food_agriculture.notes: Severe food insecurity; rain-fed agriculture; terracing tradition; recurrent drought.

energy.notes: 100% oil imported; geothermal potential in Danakil; Hirgigo thermal plant; solar projects expanding.

transport.notes: Massawa port; Italian colonial-era railway (Asmara-Massawa, partially restored); limited infrastructure.

tourism.notes: Asmara UNESCO site for Italian Art Deco and Modernist architecture; tourism heavily restricted; diaspora visitors significant.

human_rights_gender.notes: Ranked among world's worst for human rights; indefinite national service (forced labor); no free press since 2001; no elections since 1993; highest refugee outflow per capita in Africa.

security_stability.notes: Participated in Ethiopia's Tigray war (2020-22); UN sanctions lifted 2018; highly militarized society; mass exodus of youth fleeing national service.

cultural_heritage.media_landscape: No independent media; state-run EriTV and Dimtsi Hafash only; ranked last globally for press freedom
cultural_heritage.notes: 9 ethnic groups; Tigrinya and Tigre largest; Italian colonial architecture uniquely preserved; cycling culture.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Mixed: civil law, customary law, religious law
legal_system.notes: 1997 constitution never implemented; no elections held; president rules by decree; Special Court handles political cases.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Ranks last in Africa for press freedom and business environment.

current_leader.name: Isaias Afwerki
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former EPLF leader; only president since independence; no elections held; constitution never implemented; indefinite national conscription
